subject: Cerulean (ceres-3.1): Elevated 5xx wave — bridging update and next steps
body:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Acme Support <support@acmecorp.com>, Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 May 2028 00:18:00 -0700
Subject: Cerulean (ceres-3.1) — we observed elevated 5xx rates starting 00:10 PT

Hi Emma / Acme team,

We saw a sharp increase in 5xx responses from model ceres-3.1 beginning ~00:10 PT. Traffic from your production project shows a ~6% 5xx rate on generation endpoints for short-context requests. We're investigating; infra has applied a temporary circuit control to limit retries and route to the ceres-3.0 fallback.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm if you pushed any new prompts or changed request size patterns in the last hour?
- We will keep you posted on mitigation steps and timeline for full recovery.

Attachment: ceres-3.1-5xx-log-extract.txt (snippet)

— Ben
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@acmecorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 May 2028 00:34:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Cerulean (ceres-3.1) — we observed elevated 5xx rates starting 00:10 PT

Thanks Ben — we did not change prompts or payload sizes on our side. We rolled a config that increased concurrency yesterday at 10:00 PT, but that was several hours earlier and has been stable. We have a customer-facing job running now; please advise on expected impact and if you recommend us switching to ceres-3.0 full-time.

— Emma
Product Ops, Acme Corp

On Wed, May 2, 2028 at 00:50 Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Internal triage: initial logs show a KV cache mismatch combined with an optimizer failing to allocate a transient workspace under specific sequence-length patterns (mostly <128 tokens). This leads to an internal handler throwing 5xx instead of soft-failing. I kicked policy to route short requests to ceres-3.0.
>
> Olga / Marcus — can we scope whether a quantization patch in the 3.1 rollout could be a trigger? Rafael, please surface any recent kernel rollouts.
>
> — Ben

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 May 2028 01:22:40 -0700
Subject: Re: Cerulean (ceres-3.1) — triage update and short-term mitigations

Thanks — I confirmed a runtime patch (memory allocator tweak) rolled to a subset of the ceres-3.1 pool at 23:45 PT. The allocator tweak interacts poorly with the optimized KV cache path for <128 tokens; on contention it can return an EAGAIN that we're not handling gracefully.

Short-term actions taken:
- Disabled the new allocator on the affected pool (traffic slowly draining back to green).
- Forced reroute for short requests (ceres-3.0) for impacted customer projects for the next 2h.
- Ops will run a targeted regression test and a kernel rollback for the allocator patch if fail rates persist.

I'll host a bridge in 20 minutes to walk Acme through impacts and ETA for full recovery.

— Marcus
Senior MLE, Inference Runtime

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@acmecorp.com>, Acme Support <support@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 May 2028 01:42:05 -0700
Subject: RE: Cerulean (ceres-3.1) — bridging call in 20m and mitigation summary

Emma — joining the bridge at 02:05 PT. TL;DR: we've isolated the issue to a recent allocator tweak that triggers on short-context KV cache paths, causing a subset of requests to observe 5xx instead of a graceful fallback. We have rolled the allocator out of the active pool and are routing short requests to ceres-3.0.

What to expect now:
- Immediate impact: visible 5xx should decline over the next 10–30 minutes as traffic drains and reroutes.
- Near-term: we will monitor and keep your project pinned to ceres-3.0 for 24 hours unless you instruct otherwise.
- Postmortem: we will deliver an RCA and remediation plan within 72 hours and share the test artifacts and logs.

Bridge details: https://redwood.example.com/incidents/INC-20280502-17 (join pin)
Attachment: bridge-call-notes-0502.pdf (summary + action items)

Thanks for the quick confirm on your side.
— Olga
Head of Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

-----BEGIN FORWARDED MESSAGE-----
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 May 2028 15:10:22 -0700
Subject: Cerulean follow-up — regression verification and notes

Post-rollback verification notes:
- Kernel rollback and allocator disable completed at 14:30 PT on 03 May.
- Synthetic and customer load tests show 0.2% 5xx over 6k qps (within SLO range).
- Root cause: allocator tweak + a rare sequence-length/kv-cache path that surfaced under contesting GC on certain hosts.
- Remediation: revert allocator tweak permanently until a safe allocator handshake is implemented; add a defensive catch to convert EAGAIN into a soft-fail and retry path.

Deliverables: I attached extracted logs and the bridge notes. We'll ship a full RCA doc and an automated regression test case by EOD 05/05.

— Rafael
Principal Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference

On Thu, May 3, 2028 at 15:42 Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Emma / Acme team — final update: the rollback is complete and we've seen sustained low error rates for the past hour. We will keep your project pinned to ceres-3.0 for 24hrs and coordinate a test rollout with you next week when the new allocator handshake is in place.
>
> Attachments: ceres-3.1-5xx-log-extract.txt, bridge-call-notes-0502.pdf
>
> Thank you for the quick collaboration and apologies for the disruption.
>
> — Olga
> Head of Customer Operations
> Redwood Inference
